A01.name: Complexity bias
A01.rationale: Recommendation is for simplest architecture (regime-conditioned linear), not most complex

A02.name: Bigger model must be better
A02.rationale: Deep learning rejected, ensemble deferred. Linear regime model recommended.

A03.name: Data leakage disguised as regime information
A03.rationale: Regime labels are PIT_NATIVE (FRED data same-day publication)

A04.name: Regime definitions selected after observing returns
A04.rationale: Regime definition (60-day rolling median) is objectively specified, not selected based on IC

A05.name: Sample fragmentation
A05.rationale: Regime conditioning splits data ~50/50. Still ~1000 observations per regime — adequate but noted.

A06.name: False interaction discovery
A06.rationale: Phase 36-R showed regime differentials in exploratory testing. Phase 37-R will confirm.

A07.name: Overlapping-label inflation
A07.rationale: Forward returns properly lagged. No overlapping labels.

A08.name: Multiple-model fishing
A08.rationale: Only one model class recommended (regime-conditioned linear). No model comparison.

A09.name: Hyperparameter explosion
A09.rationale: Alpha=1.0 locked from Phase 36-R. No tuning.

A10.name: Data sufficiency illusion
A10.rationale: ~2000 independent time periods adequate for linear models. Deep learning rejected for data insufficiency.

A11.name: Raw observations confused with independent samples
A11.rationale: Data sufficiency audit uses effective independent observations (~2000 periods), not raw rows (~100K)

A12.name: Deep learning hype bias
A12.rationale: Deep learning explicitly rejected with detailed justification

A13.name: Ensemble overfitting
A13.rationale: Ensemble deferred — no evidence of complementarity

A14.name: Using protected OOS information indirectly
A14.rationale: No OOS data accessed. Recommendations based on exploratory evidence only.

A15.name: Modifying future priorities based on confirmatory OOS data
A15.rationale: OOS status is DATA_NOT_READY. No confirmatory data used.

A16.name: Recommending without identifying capability gap
A16.rationale: Capability gaps explicitly identified: regime switching, conditional nonlinear, temporal dependencies

A17.name: Recommending complexity when simpler model suffices

A18.name: Treating exploratory evidence as confirmation
A18.rationale: Phase 36-R evidence explicitly labeled as exploratory. Phase 37-R registration acknowledges pending confirmatory test.

A19.name: Ignoring failed model classes
A19.rationale: All evaluated model classes documented with reasons for rejection

A20.name: Ignoring computational constraints
A20.rationale: Compute assessment confirms current infrastructure sufficient for justified models
